web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Price Is What It Is — Reverse DCF and Relative Valuation
question: What growth and margin assumptions are already priced into Yash Highvoltage at ₹1,240.85 (60.3x TTM P/E), and how does it stack up against Indian T&D peers?

epigraph.quote: A high trailing multiple is neither cheap nor expensive on its own; it is simply a compressed statement of how long high incremental returns on capital must endure.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Principle

web_blocks.title: 7.1 Reverse DCF: What ₹1,240.85 Implies About the Next Decade

web_blocks.html: At the November 13, 2026 close of ₹1,240.85, Yash Highvoltage carries a ₹3,709.75 crore market cap [19]. Subtracting ₹95 crore of net cash (₹95.6 Cr cash vs. ₹10.3 Cr debt) leaves an Enterprise Value (EV) of ₹3,615 crore [1][19]. On TTM numbers, the stock trades at 60.32x P/E and 11.6x P/B [19]. Those multiples rest on 25.04% ROE, 24.52% operating margin, 70.82% TTM sales growth, and 102.67% TTM EPS growth [19].

Why does the market pay 60.3x trailing earnings for a small-cap bushing maker? The driver is Yash's sharp H1 FY27 earnings inflection [1][3]. In H1 FY27, revenue rose 95% YoY to ₹194.5 crore, while EBITDA reached ₹54.7 crore (28.1% margin) [1][3]. PAT surged 165% YoY to ₹36.2 crore, nearly matching full-year FY26 PAT of ₹37.4 crore in six months [1][3]. Annualizing H1 PAT implies ~₹72.4 crore for FY27, or ~₹75–80 crore with H2 weighting [1]. That run-rate compresses forward P/E from 60.3x TTM down to roughly 46–49x FY27E [1][19].

web_blocks.takeaway: At ₹1,240.85, the market is pricing in ~24% annualized FCF compounding over a decade—demanding execution on Jarod Phase 2, but well below the 38% FY22–FY26 revenue CAGR and 95% H1 FY27 surge [1][19].

web_blocks.html: Our Reverse DCF shows that ₹1,240.85 is neither deep value nor an untethered bubble. We model a 12.5% discount rate and a 5.5% terminal growth rate on ₹55–60 crore of normalized FY27E FCF (ex-Jarod capex). At EV ₹3,615 crore, the market prices in a ~23%–25% 10-year FCF CAGR. Management's Jarod math (~4x turn on ₹220 Cr capex, or ₹800+ Cr revenue) and the ₹760 crore order book bridge credibly to ₹650–750 crore of sales by FY30–FY31 [1][2]. Still, that 24% CAGR is already in the price. There is zero margin of safety if Jarod Phase 2 slips or DSO climbs.

web_blocks.title: 7.2 Multiple Bands & Rerating Mechanics Since the 2024 IPO

web_blocks.html: Since its December 2024 BSE SME listing, Yash has undergone a textbook quality rerating [10][19]. Early post-IPO trading valued the stock at 25x–30x trailing earnings when OIP share was larger and working capital absorbed half of profits [1][10]. Over the past year (+157.44% 1Y return), three catalysts lifted the multiple to 60.32x TTM P/E [19]. First, RIP bushings hit 86% of H1 FY27 revenue, expanding gross margin +800 bps from 40.3% (FY24) to 48.3% (H1 FY27) [1]. Second, H1 FY27 CFO jumped to ₹45.2 crore (125% of PAT), proving scale drives cash conversion [1]. Third, the June 2026 ₹151 crore preferential issue brought WhiteOak, ValueQuest, Motilal Oswal, and Malabar onto the register [1][6].

Paying 60x trailing earnings requires separating peak-cycle multiples from inflection-year multiples. In cyclical commodities, 60x earnings is dangerous because margins mean-revert. Here, TTM P/E still blends H2 FY26 (₹23.7 Cr PAT) with H1 FY27 (₹36.2 Cr PAT) [1]. Meanwhile, the ₹319.6 crore equity base already holds cash raised for Phase 2 550 kV lines that earn zero revenue today [1]. If PAT compounds at 35%–40% over FY27–FY29, the multiple compresses naturally to 31x–35x. Conversely, any two-quarter dispatch hiccup could reset a 60x multiple down to 40x–45x within weeks.

That asymmetry explains why entry price matters so much at this stage. Waiting for a pullback toward ₹1,085–₹1,145 trims the effective entry multiple by roughly 8% to 13% without sacrificing exposure to the FY28 earnings ramp. It also keeps risk anchored to a clean technical support shelf rather than open-air momentum.

web_blocks.caption: Yash Highvoltage vs. Listed Indian T&D Equipment Peers (As of Nov 13, 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: YASHHV commands a premium P/E (60.32x) to transformer OEMs TARIL (31.04x) and VOLTAMP (31.43x) because its 24.52% TTM operating margin and 25.04% ROE reflect a pure-play condenser-bushing duopoly rather than bulk transformer assembly, while trading at a discount to CGPOWER (94.88x) [19][20][21][22][23].

web_blocks.html: Comparing Yash with four listed Indian T&D peers explains its valuation band [19][20][21][22][23]. Transformers & Rectifiers India (TARIL) at ₹314.80 (₹9,449 Cr MCap) trades at 31.04x P/E with 23.3% ROCE and 19.1% ROE [20][26]. Voltamp Transformers (VOLTAMP) at ₹9,849.00 (₹9,964 Cr MCap) trades at 31.43x P/E with 23.5% ROCE and 17.4% ROE [21][27]. Both are bulk transformer OEMs facing raw-material pass-through swings and 12%–18% operating margins. Notably, Voltamp trades below both its 50-day SMA (₹10,443.84) and 30-week SMA (₹10,183.60) [21].

At the top end, CG Power (CGPOWER) at ₹828.00 (₹1,30,451 Cr MCap) trades at 94.88x P/E with 26.7% ROCE and 20.5% ROE [22][28]. APAR Industries (APARINDS) at ₹14,667.00 (₹61,418 Cr MCap) trades at 43.05x P/E with 31.8% ROCE and 20.3% ROE [23][29]. Yash sits in the sweet spot. Its 24.52% TTM operating margin and 25.04% ROE beat TARIL and Voltamp by 500–800 bps [19][20][21]. Unlike APAR (also below its 50D and 30W SMAs) [23], Yash holds 0.05x debt-to-equity and an 8-to-10-year utility approval moat [1][19].

web_blocks.title: 7.4 Cycle & Valuation Parallel: Hitachi Energy India (2021–2025)

web_blocks.mechanism: As India's grid modernization and HVDC/substation capex accelerated, Hitachi Energy India traded persistently between 60x and 90x trailing P/E even before margins expanded, because investors priced in multi-year backlog conversion and localization of high-voltage components.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Order backlog expanded >2.5x from ~₹4,700 Cr (FY22) to >₹18,000 Cr (FY25); EBITDA margins expanded from ~6% to >11%, and the stock compounded >4x from ~₹2,500 to >₹11,000 despite 'expensive' 70x+ trailing P/E prints along the way.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: In specialized high-voltage grid equipment with multi-year qualification barriers, selling solely because trailing P/E crosses 55x–60x misses the earnings catch-up—provided the order book converts without margin dilution and working capital stays disciplined.

web_blocks.caption: FY28E PAT vs. Forward P/E Sensitivity (2.9897 Cr Shares; Implied Share Price & Return vs. CMP ₹1,240.85)
web_blocks.takeaway: At ₹90 Cr FY28E PAT, 35x implies ₹1,054/share (-15.1% vs. CMP); sustaining 45x–50x requires 25–28% EBITDA margins and on-time H2 FY27 Jarod Phase 2 commissioning without DSO slippage.

web_blocks.html: The sensitivity grid makes clear why paying ₹1,240.85 leaves no margin of safety. Across 2.9897 crore shares, 35x on ₹90 crore FY28E PAT equals ₹3,150 crore (₹1,054/share), or -15.1% below CMP [19]. Sustaining a 45x–50x multiple is achievable ONLY if YASHHV holds 25%–28% EBITDA margins—far above bulk transformer OEMs TARIL and VOLTAMP (14%–19% margins at ~31x P/E) [19][20][21]—and commissions Jarod Phase 2 in H2 FY27 without DSO or gross-margin slippage [1]. Waiting for support at ₹1,085–₹1,145 anchors entry near the 35x–38x Base valuation band [19].

Valuation Trigger: We upgrade fair-value sensitivity toward ₹1,580–₹1,850 if Q3/Q4 FY27 Jarod indigenous RIP core commissioning lifts FY28E PAT above ₹105 crore with DSO below 65 days and gross margin >=44%; conversely, we cut fair value toward ₹880–₹1,050 if gross margin falls below 44% or DSO exceeds 75 days.

book_paragraphs: Once you and I finish auditing a company's business quality and forensic cash flows, we finally earn the right to look at the stock price. And when we look at Yash Highvoltage at ₹1,240.85 per share, the first number that jumps off the screen is 60.32x trailing twelve-month earnings. For a company with a ₹3,709.75 crore market capitalization, that multiple immediately splits investors into two camps: momentum buyers who ignore valuation completely, and value purists who close the file at 60x P/E.

Both reactions are lazy. Instead of guessing whether 60x is expensive, you and I should run a Reverse Discounted Cash Flow—asking what the market is actually assuming about the next ten years at ₹1,240.85, and then checking those implied assumptions against the physical capacity and order book we audited in Chapters 5 and 6.

book_subsections.title: What the Reverse DCF Actually Prices In
paragraphs: Let us do the arithmetic together cleanly. At ₹1,240.85 per share, Yash's market cap is ₹3,709.75 crore. Subtract ₹95 crore of net cash on the September 2026 balance sheet, and the Enterprise Value is roughly ₹3,615 crore. Now look at why the trailing P/E of 60.32x is slightly deceptive: it blends H2 FY26, when PAT was ₹23.7 crore, with H1 FY27, when PAT surged 165% year-on-year to ₹36.2 crore. Annualizing that first-half run-rate puts FY27 earnings around ₹72 to ₹80 crore, which brings the forward multiple down to 46 to 49 times.

If we apply a 12.5% cost of equity and a 5.5% terminal growth rate to a normalized FY27 maintenance free cash flow base of ₹55 to ₹60 crore, the current ₹3,615 crore Enterprise Value implies roughly 23% to 25% annualized free cash flow growth over the next ten years. Compare that 24% implied hurdle to what Yash is actually delivering: 38% revenue CAGR over FY22–FY26, 95% revenue growth in H1 FY27, a ₹760 crore order book, and a ₹220 crore Jarod greenfield plant designed for 4x asset turnover.

The conclusion is balanced and nuanced. The market is not hallucinating—if Yash reaches ₹650 to ₹750 crore in revenue at an 18% net margin by FY30, earnings of ₹115 to ₹135 crore compress the multiple into the low thirties. At the same time, paying 60x trailing earnings leaves zero cushion for execution delays. You are paying for smooth Jarod Phase 2 commissioning upfront, which is why our entry discipline must be anchored to technical support rather than chased in open air.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: When a stock trades at 60x trailing earnings during a genuine capacity inflection, the danger isn't that the business is bad—it's that any two-quarter delay in factory commissioning turns a smooth rerating into a sharp 25% multiple reset.

book_subsections.title: Multiple Bands, Pre-Funded Equity, and Inflection-Year Compression
paragraphs: It also helps to trace how the market's multiple evolved since the December 2024 BSE SME IPO. Early on, Yash traded around 25x to 30x trailing earnings because oil-impregnated paper bushings still made up a hefty share of sales and working capital absorbed nearly half of cumulative profits. Over the past twelve months, the stock returned 157.44% as three structural proofs arrived back-to-back: RIP bushings reached 86% of H1 FY27 revenue, operating cash flow jumped to 125% of net profit, and marquee institutional funds stepped into the June 2026 ₹151 crore preferential issue.

Notice the crucial distinction between a peak-cycle multiple and an inflection-year multiple. In a commodity cycle, 60x earnings is a trap because margins are about to collapse. At Yash, the ₹319.6 crore equity base already includes the cash raised for Phase 2 indigenous 550 kV core lines before those lines have booked their first rupee of revenue. That means P/B of 11.6x and TTM P/E of 60.3x are carrying pre-funded growth capacity on the denominator. Once Jarod Phase 1 and Phase 2 ramp toward full utilization, backward integration of RIP cores should protect gross margins near the 46% to 48% band while operating leverage absorbs fixed plant overhead.

book_subsections.title: Benchmarking Against Indian T&D Peers
paragraphs: To see why Yash commands a higher multiple than traditional transformer makers, you and I only need to line it up against four listed Indian peers. Transformers & Rectifiers India (TARIL) trades at 31.04x P/E with 23.3% ROCE and 19.1% ROE on a ₹9,449 crore market cap, and Voltamp Transformers trades at 31.43x P/E with 23.5% ROCE and 17.4% ROE on a ₹9,964 crore market cap. Both are fine industrial businesses, yet both carry lower operating margins because bulk transformer assembly passes through copper and CRGO steel fluctuations.

Yash, by contrast, operates in a specialized condenser-bushing niche with 24.52% TTM operating margins and 25.04% ROE, nearly debt-free at 0.05x debt-to-equity. Meanwhile, CG Power trades at 94.88x P/E with 26.7% ROCE and 20.5% ROE on a ₹1,30,451 crore market cap, and APAR Industries trades at 43.05x P/E with 31.8% ROCE and 20.3% ROE on a ₹61,418 crore market cap. Crucially, both Voltamp and APAR are currently sitting below their 50-day and 30-week moving averages. Yash's premium over TARIL and Voltamp is earned by its margin structure, cash conversion, and 8-to-10-year utility qualification moat, not merely market froth.

book_subsections.title: The Hitachi Energy India Valuation Parallel
paragraphs: Before we dismiss a 60x multiple out of hand, consider a concrete Indian grid-equipment parallel: Hitachi Energy India between 2021 and 2025. Throughout the early stages of India's substation and HVDC cycle, Hitachi Energy traded between 60x and 90x trailing earnings—a level that kept traditional value investors on the sidelines for years. Yet as its order backlog swelled more than two-and-a-half times from ₹4,700 crore to over ₹18,000 crore and localized manufacturing lifted EBITDA margins from 6% toward 11%+, earnings caught up to the multiple and the stock multiplied more than fourfold.

The lesson for you and me is clear: in specialized high-voltage grid equipment, high trailing multiples can persist as long as backlog conversion and margin expansion remain intact. Our job is not to short a 60x compounder—it is to refuse to chase it blindly above support, demanding a favorable entry shelf where risk-reward tilts decisively in our favor.

book_subsections.title: Sensitivity Check: 30x–50x Forward Multiples and What Justifies 45x–50x
paragraphs: Every Reverse DCF is only as honest as its downside sensitivity. Across Yash's 2.9897 crore shares, let us test FY28E PAT of ₹80 crore, ₹90 crore, and ₹105 crore across 30x, 35x, 45x, and 50x P/E multiples. At ₹90 crore of FY28E PAT, a 30x multiple yields ₹2,700 crore (₹903 per share, -27.2% vs. CMP), while 35x yields ₹3,150 crore (₹1,054 per share, -15.1% vs. CMP). Even at ₹105 crore of FY28E PAT, 35x puts fair value at ₹1,229 per share—virtually flat against today's ₹1,240.85 price.

That math explains why a 45x to 50x forward multiple—which lifts ₹90 crore to ₹105 crore of FY28E PAT to ₹1,355–₹1,756 per share—is achievable ONLY if Yash sustains 25% to 28% EBITDA margins (compared with 14% to 19% for transformer OEMs TARIL and VOLTAMP at 31x P/E) and commissions Jarod Phase 2 in H2 FY27 without DSO or gross-margin slippage. Waiting for ₹1,085 to ₹1,145 aligns your entry with both fundamental support and technical support.

book_subsections.title: Capital Allocation Math: How Jarod Phase 2 Reshapes Unit Economics
paragraphs: Before we leave valuation, let us examine one subtle detail that most surface-level P/E screens completely miss: the balance-sheet impact of Yash's June 2026 ₹151 crore preferential issue. When a company raises ₹91 crore in equity and issues ₹60 crore in warrants ahead of building a new factory, the denominator of Return on Equity swells overnight from ₹41.7 crore in March 2024 to ₹319.6 crore in September 2026. That is why ROE naturally moderated from 40.4% in FY23 to 25.04% today, even as operating margins expanded.

Here is why that matters for your valuation model. Out of the ₹220 crore Jarod greenfield outlay, ₹106 crore had already been deployed by September 2026, leaving ₹114 crore of capex to deploy alongside ₹95 crore of net cash already sitting in fixed deposits. Management guides for roughly 4x asset turnover on incremental greenfield capex once Jarod hits full utilization. On ₹220 crore of gross block, 4x turnover implies ₹880 crore of incremental revenue capacity over time—more than triple FY26's ₹235.1 crore base.

Moreover, Phase 2 brings 550 kV Resin Impregnated Paper core winding in-house. Previously, importing high-voltage RIP cores forced Yash to carry ₹66.7 crore to ₹71.8 crore of buffer inventory and absorbed half of cumulative operating cash flow between FY22 and FY26. Once indigenous cores come online in H2 FY27 and scale through FY28, both gross margins and inventory turns should structurally improve—turning what looks like an expensive 60.32x trailing multiple today into a self-funding 30x–35x forward multiple by FY29.

book_subsections.title: Why EV-to-Sales and Forward Earnings Tell a Cleaner Story Than P/B
paragraphs: Many retail screeners glance at Yash Highvoltage's 11.6x price-to-book ratio and immediately assume the stock is priced like a software monopoly. That comparison misses how balance-sheet timing distorts book value. Remember that Yash holds roughly ₹95 crore of net cash against ₹10.3 crore of total borrowings, and its shareholders' funds jumped from ₹41.73 crore in March 2024 to ₹319.60 crore in September 2026 largely because of two equity raises totaling over ₹220 crore.

When you strip out ₹95 crore of net cash to arrive at a ₹3,615 crore Enterprise Value, and divide by annualized H1 FY27 revenue of ₹389 crore, Yash trades at roughly 9.3x trailing-annualized sales—or closer to 5.5x to 6.5x FY29 revenue if Jarod scales toward ₹600 crore. That is still a full valuation that demands flawless execution, which is why we refuse to chase open-air prices, yet it is grounded in 28.1% EBITDA margins and 25.04% return on equity rather than empty hype.

book_subsections.title: Why Margin Durability Matters More Than Near-Term P/E
paragraphs: When you compare Yash Highvoltage at 60.32x trailing earnings against TARIL at 31.04x or Voltamp at 31.43x, ask yourself one decisive question: what happens if transformer demand pauses for two quarters? A bulk transformer assembler with 14% operating margins and heavy copper pass-through sees its earnings swing sharply. By contrast, a condenser-bushing specialist whose RIP product mix just hit 86% of revenue and whose aftermarket retrofit business carries >96% repeat orders enjoys far stickier gross margins near 46% to 48%.

That margin resilience is what justifies a structural valuation premium over time—provided Yash keeps its receivable days disciplined and brings Jarod Phase 2 online without cost overruns. You are not paying 60x for commodity metal bending; you are paying for an 8-to-10-year utility qualification bottleneck.

book_subsections.title: Translating Forward Multiples Into Concrete Earnings Milestones
paragraphs: To keep your valuation anchor practical over the next eight quarters, remember that Yash Highvoltage does not need heroic multiple expansion to reward shareholders from a ₹1,085 to ₹1,145 support entry. If revenue scales from ₹235.1 crore in FY26 toward ₹390 crore in FY27 and ₹500 to ₹550 crore in FY28 as Jarod ramps up, even a modest 18% net margin delivers ₹90 to ₹105 crore in FY28 net profit. At a 45x to 50x forward multiple—which is actually a contraction from today’s 60.32x trailing P/E—the stock reaches ₹1,505 to ₹1,580 naturally through earnings compounding alone.
